title: Trip the mint trap on a test-writing cell that cites no contract decision
action:
Per D4 (plan.md, Approach, S5): a test-writing cell that cites NO contract decision is refused - the mint trap. Without it, a contract nobody logged reads exactly like 'there is no contract', and the worker mints one by writing tests against it. This cell adds the trap beside the tripwire the previous cell built, and nothing else.

Step 1 - the signal, with its limits, not around them. There is NO cell field marking a test-writing cell (verbs/cells/validate.rs:230-473). Two arms:
(a) ARMED, can refuse: the cell declares a test-shaped path in files, or carries role 'test'. Do NOT invent globs - reuse path_looks_like_test (verbs/cells/finish_support.rs:693), which already covers a bare test/tests path segment and .test. filenames and carries its own anti-false-positive notes. Measured on the 92 live cells this fires on 30 with 0 false positives; role 'test' fires on 0 today and the role vocabulary is deliberately open and never membership-checked (validate.rs:43,48), so treat role as an additional trigger, never as the signal.
(b) ADVISORY, warns and never refuses: any other cell whose title or action names test writing. That is 67 of 92 cells - too soft to refuse on, loud enough to say.
Name the hole in the code's own doc comment: a role 'code' cell adding a #[cfg(test)] module inside a source file it was already touching is the DOMINANT test-writing shape in this repo and the armed arm cannot see it. That is accepted and recorded, not hidden.

Step 2 - 'cites no contract decision' is precise, not 'cites nothing'. A cell trips the trap when NONE of its cell.decisions entries resolves to a store decision carrying a tag in the contract:<name> namespace. Reuse the citation resolver and the tag read from verbs/decisions/read.rs; a local D-ID resolves to nothing and therefore does not satisfy the requirement. A cell citing a real store decision that carries no contract tag also does not satisfy it.

Step 3 - the ramp, exactly as logged (decision d853e4c6, relation touches:9c0104e0). The refusal ships fully built, but while the ACTIVE decision set holds zero decisions tagged in the contract: namespace, the armed arm WARNS instead of refusing - in that state no cell can satisfy the rule, and a rule nobody can satisfy is a dead workflow rather than a guard. The moment the first contract:<name> decision exists, the armed arm refuses. Derive that condition from the same active-decision read the tripwire already uses; do NOT add a config switch, a flag, or a stored counter - a second thing to forget to update is exactly what D1 refuses. Follow the warn-then-refuse wording already in this function: NO_ROUTE_RECORD at handlers_write.rs:1465-1471 warns once per session, then refuses; match its voice, and say in the warn text what will make it start refusing.

Step 4 - placement. Same door, same block as the previous cell's tripwire in claim_cell_cross_session_ex, pre-store-lock, zero mutation on refusal, release_claim before returning. The trap and the tripwire are two rules over the same walk - share the read, keep the two refusals separately named so one red proof says which rule fired.

Step 5 - tests in verbs/cells/tests.rs; judge existing coverage first and author only the gap. REFUSE cases (with at least one contract: decision in the fixture store, so the ramp is armed): a cell with a test-shaped path in files and no citation; the same with role 'test' and no test-shaped path; a cell citing a store decision that carries no contract tag. ALLOW cases: a cell with a test-shaped path that DOES cite a contract-tagged decision; a cell with no test-shaped path and no citation; the named hole - a role 'code' cell whose files are source-only, which must PASS, with the test's own name saying that this is the accepted hole. RAMP cases: with zero contract: decisions in the store the same refuse-case cell claims successfully and emits the warning; after one contract: decision is added it is refused. Every refusal leaves the cell open and unclaimed - assert the record.

Step 6 - extend docs/knowledge/areas/workflow-state/dispatch.md: the trap, both arms, the ramp and what flips it, and the named hole with its measurement. Do not restate the tripwire the previous cell documented there; point at it.
